subject: Definition 2.1 (odd bimodule)
object: odd A_LR-bimodule, Ad(s) = -1 with s=(1,-1,-1,1)

subject: Lemma 2.2
object: an odd bimodule is a representation of the reduction B=(A_LR tensor A_LR^0)_p

subject: Definition 2.3 (contragredient bimodule)
object: M^0, the complex conjugate bimodule with a·xi-bar·b = conj(b* xi a*)

subject: Proposition 2.4
object: dimension of M_F is 32 and M_F is isomorphic to its contragredient M_F^0 via J_F

subject: Lemma 2.5
object: B = (A_LR tensor A_LR^0)_p is a direct sum of 4 copies of M_2(C) plus M_6(C), with irreducible representations of total dimension 32

subject: Definition 2.7 (real structure of KO-dimension n)
object: antilinear isometry J with J^2 = epsilon, JD = epsilon' DJ, sign table indexed by n mod 8

subject: Definition 2.8 (Omega^1_D)
object: the A-bimodule of sums a_j[D,b_j]

subject: Definition 2.9 (inner fluctuations of the metric)
object: D_A = D + A + epsilon' J A J^{-1} with self-adjoint A in Omega^1_D

subject: Proposition 2.11
object: up to automorphism of A_LR there is a unique maximal subalgebra A_F admitting off-diagonal Dirac operators, namely C + H + M_3(C)

subject: Lemma 2.12
object: conditions on off-diagonal Dirac operators for a subalgebra of A_LR (disjoint restrictions obstruct; otherwise a pair of minimal projections and an operator T exist)

subject: Definition 2.13 (SU(A_F))
object: subgroup of U(A_F) with determinant 1 on H_F

subject: Proposition 2.16
object: SU(A_F) is isomorphic up to a finite abelian group to U(1) x SU(2) x SU(3)

subject: Definition 2.20 (Dirac operator on H_F)
object: self-adjoint D commuting with J_F and C_F, anticommuting with gamma_F, satisfying order-one condition

subject: Theorem 2.21 (part 1)
object: every Dirac operator on H_F has the form D(Y) for 3x3 matrices Y with Y_R symmetric

subject: Theorem 2.21 (part 2)
object: all operators D(Y) with Y_R symmetric are Dirac operators

subject: Theorem 2.21 (part 3)
object: D(Y) and D(Y') are unitarily conjugate (commuting with A_F, gamma_F, J_F) iff there exist unitaries V_j, W_j with the stated transformation of Y

subject: Remark 2.23
object: unbroken colour, obtained from the classification of Dirac operators in Section 2

subject: Lemma 2.22
object: block-form characterisation of operators P in the commutant A'_F on H_F

subject: Proposition 2.24
object: moduli space C_3 as the double coset (U(3) x U(3)) \ (GL_3(C) x GL_3(C)) / U(3), of real dimension 10

subject: Lemma 2.26
object: equivalence of pairs (delta_up, C delta_down C*) with existence of diagonal unitaries A, B such that AC = C'B

subject: Lemma 2.27
object: moduli space C_1 as a quotient involving symmetric complex 3x3 matrices, real dimension 21, fibring over C_3

subject: Proposition 2.29
object: the pairing <e,f> = Tr(gamma e J f J^{-1}) is antisymmetric on K_0 x K_0, and K_0(A_F) is free abelian on e_1, e_2, f_3

subject: Proposition 2.30
object: H_F splits as H_F^(1) plus H_F^(3), each irreducible in the generic case, with the pairing matrices given in (2.48)

subject: Corollary 2.31
object: the pairing K_0 x K_0 -> R plus R is non-degenerate

subject: Remark 2.32
object: Corollary 2.31 (KO-homology generated by two elements, not singly generated over K_0)

subject: Proposition 3.1
object: A_J = {x in A : xJ = Jx} is a commutative real subalgebra of the centre, and (A_J, H, D) is a real spectral triple

subject: Lemma 3.2
object: the real part of A_F is R embedded as (lambda, lambda, lambda), and the real part of C^infty(M, A_F) is C^infty(M, R)

subject: Proposition 3.4 (part 1)
object: a unitary U commuting with gamma and J that normalises A induces a unique diffeomorphism phi with U f U* = f o phi on A_J

subject: Proposition 3.5
object: the discrete part A^(0,1) of the inner fluctuations is parameterised by an arbitrary quaternion-valued function H = phi_1 + phi_2 j

subject: Proposition 3.9 (part 1)
object: unimodular gauge potentials are parameterised by a U(1) field B, an SU(2) field W and an SU(3) field V

subject: Definition 3.8 (unimodular gauge potential)
object: A is unimodular iff Tr(A) = 0

subject: Proposition 3.11
object: Propositions 3.5 and 3.9 (parameterisation of the unimodular inner fluctuations by phi_1, phi_2, B, W, V)

subject: Lemma 3.12
object: D_A^2 = nabla* nabla - E, with nabla the connection nabla^s + A and E given by the stated expression

subject: Theorem 3.13
object: the leading terms of the spectral action S, with coefficients 48 f_4 Lambda^4, f_2 Lambda^2 and f_0 for the cosmological and Einstein-Hilbert parts

subject: Remark 3.7
object: the coefficients a and b in (3.16) are identified with Y_2(S) and H(S) of [1]

subject: Introduction, item 1 (gauge coupling relation)
object: g_2 = g_3 = sqrt(5/3) g_1 at the unification scale, as in GUT models

subject: Introduction, item 3 (mass relation)
object: sum over generations of m_e^2 + m_nu^2 + 3 m_d^2 + 3 m_u^2 = 8 M_W^2 at the unification scale

subject: Introduction, item 2 (Higgs mass)
object: the Higgs scattering parameter alpha_h at the unification scale, with renormalisation group running

subject: Introduction (renormalisability of the gravity part)
object: renormalisation analysis of higher-derivative gravity as in [12] and [21]

subject: Introduction (Einstein-Hilbert action)
object: for classical Riemannian manifolds the spectral action (1.3) gives the Einstein-Hilbert action of pure gravity
